claims.text: A StatefulSet with N replicas names its Pods <statefulset name>-<ordinal>, ordinals 0..N-1 (db-0 for the StatefulSet db with replicas: 1); a Pod that replaces a deleted one gets the same name and ordinal.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Workloads > StatefulSets > Pod Identity (Ordinal Index, Stable Network ID); statefulset-db.txt (db-0 again after delete)

claims.text: A StatefulSet replacement Pod is a new Pod; nothing keeps the old Pod's IP address for it (docs: IPs 'may have changed'); the stable identity is the name and the claim. Output at stage-3: 'same IP address as before: no'.

volumeClaimTemplates: the StatefulSet controller creates one PVC per Pod named <template name>-<statefulset name>-<ordinal> (data-db-0) and mounts it into that Pod as the volume of the template's name; a rescheduled/replacement Pod mounts the existing PVC of the same name.

Default podManagementPolicy OrderedReady: Pods are created in order 0..N-1, each only after all predecessors are Running and Ready; on scale-down Pods are terminated in reverse order, highest ordinal first.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: StatefulSets > Deployment and Scaling Guarantees; Pod Management Policies

claims.text: By default (persistentVolumeClaimRetentionPolicy whenDeleted/whenScaled = Retain) deleting a StatefulSet or scaling it down does not delete its PVCs; scaling up again or recreating the StatefulSet with the same name reuses the PVC of the same name (data-db-1, data-db-0).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: StatefulSets > PersistentVolumeClaim retention; Stable Storage (PVCs not deleted when Pods or StatefulSet deleted)

claims.text: A claim with no storageClassName gets the cluster default StorageClass; in kind that is standard, which keeps the volume on one node (k8s.l2.storage-classes). Output: data-db-0 Bound, 1Gi, RWO, STORAGECLASS standard.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Default StorageClass; db.yaml lines 59-61 comment; statefulset-db.txt

claims.text: The postgres image runs the scripts in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d only when the data directory is empty; on start with an existing database it logs 'PostgreSQL Database directory appears to contain a database; Skipping initialization'.
claims.source_hint: Docker Official Image postgres docs: Initialization scripts; statefulset-db.txt last lines; db.yaml lines 48-49

claims.text: With an emptyDir, a replacement db Pod starts on an empty folder, so the init scripts of db-init seed the 12 orders again and rows written since are lost (k8s.l2.persistent-volume-claims outline item 1; db-init seeds 12 orders).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Volumes > emptyDir; examples/don-hang base/db-init.yaml lines 55-126 at stage-3

claims.text: A Deployment's Pod template has no per-Pod claim: all its Pods name the same claim, including the new Pod the default RollingUpdate starts before stopping the old one (replicas 1: maxSurge 25% rounds up to 1, maxUnavailable rounds down to 0).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Deployments > Strategy > Rolling Update (Max Surge, Max Unavailable); k8s.l1.rolling-updates

claims.text: A second replica (db-1) would get its own new claim data-db-1, run db-init on its empty folder (12 seeded orders) and receive nothing written to db-0: a StatefulSet does not replicate data; PostgreSQL replication needs its own configuration, absent from db.yaml.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: StatefulSets (no data replication; Stable Storage); PostgreSQL 17 docs: High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication; base/db.yaml at stage-3

claims.text: A Service sends connections to any ready Pod matching its selector: Service db (selector app: db) would reach both db-0 and db-1 with replicas: 2.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Services (selector, EndpointSlices of ready Pods); base/db.yaml lines 71-82

claims.text: base/db.yaml at stage-3: StatefulSet db, replicas 1, label app: db (L6-24); mounts data at /var/lib/postgresql/data (L53-54); volumes lists only init-scripts (L55-58); volumeClaimTemplates data, RWO, 1Gi, no storageClassName (L62-69); Service db kept (L71-82).

statefulset-db.sh at stage-3: L19-33 commit base/db.yaml replacing the Deployment db (emptyDir), wait for Argo CD sync, print data-db-0, count orders; db_ip/orders defined L8-9; L38-45 save IP, delete db-0, wait, list, compare IP, count, grep log.
Output at stage-3: before: deployment.apps/db; data-db-0 Bound pvc-... 1Gi RWO standard; orders 12; after deleting db-0: db-0 1/1 Running, same IP: no, orders 12, log 'Skipping initialization'.
Try it: after kubectl delete pod db-0, kubectl get pvc data-db-0 shows the same VOLUME, Bound, with an AGE older than the new Pod's.
Opinion: a database that must survive Pod replacement wants a fixed Pod-to-volume pairing, which a StatefulSet gives and a Deployment does not.

beyond_scope: Postgres image skips /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d when the data directory is not empty — needed to explain why orders stay 12 and nothing is re-seeded; Service db reaching both Pods with replicas: 2 — to make outline item 6 concrete.
